Check the actual track text at the venue. If it is not about chaos→order, cut the chaos slides to ten seconds: "we indexed 53,557 manuals from 84 portals — and none of them is the one a professional needs."

slides.title: 53,557 rows. 84 portals.
slides.caption: Every one of them a different shape.
notes: "So we went and indexed every manual a manufacturer publishes. Fifty-three thousand five hundred and fifty-seven rows, across eighty-four different portals."
Twenty-five thousand of those rows point at a file another row already named.
*Do not say "53,557 manuals"* — they are rows, and 25,357 of them are the same file under another year. Say rows, then say 14,770 distinct PDFs. The honesty is the pitch.

slides.text: It is a PDF in his Dropbox, in a folder with four hundred scanned bulletins, the importer's emails and three photos of a wiring loom.
slides.sub: He connects the folder once. Every PDF he drops in from then on gets *the exact same treatment as a factory manual* — read page by page, its own headings become the search index, and every quote is searched back into the PDF's text layer. *If we can't find the ink, we don't draw the marker.*
notes: "Nothing is rewritten. Nothing is uploaded anywhere else. It is his document, in his index, and the answer is still a page he can hold a judge to."

Why Dropbox and not a watched directory: longpoll gives sub-second change notice without a token on the socket and without polling a laptop that is asleep; content_hash tells us the same manual saved twice is the same manual before we spend ten cents; and the folder works from his phone in the workshop and his desktop in the office.
The abstraction is one Store-shaped seam. If the next shop is on Drive, that is a second adapter, not a second product.

If it says `unmatched`: the name is the metadata. Rename to `<make> <model> <year>.pdf` and re-drop. *Say it out loud — refusing to guess is the feature.*

"Is that a real service manual?" Yes: MV Agusta publishes its workshop manuals free and 113 are in our registry. We are not showing a BMW one, because BMW charges nine euros an hour and we do not fetch metered documents.

slides.title: One poller, one webhook, one ingest
slides.caption: The manual he already bought takes the same path as a factory PDF. A file that does not parse comes back unmatched.
notes: *Do not read the diagram.* Three sentences: one poller, one webhook, one ingest. The Dropbox side is four documented calls and a stored cursor. The moment the bytes are on disk it is the same function that ingests a factory PDF.
Longpoll is unauthenticated *by design* — the cursor is the credential — so our watcher never puts the token on an eight-minute socket. That is a good line.

Honest gaps: cross-tenant dedupe is *not* built — the content hash is stored, the dedupe is not. And there is no per-shop tenancy boundary yet; the manual id already ends -shop precisely so the free -om row survives underneath it.

slides.title: What the model is allowed to do
slides.line: Emit page numbers. That's all. *The server cuts the quote out of the page.*
points: 100% of 48 claim sentences carry a page
100% of 43 quotes verbatim on the page they name
slides.caption: Same rule on his document as on the factory's.
notes: The grounding gate is the load-bearing part: `ingest/ground.py` drops any quote it cannot find in the PDF's text layer.
Every screen shows the manual's cover title and its own printed page number, so there is no way to read an answer here without knowing who wrote it.
The registry stores *locations, not documents* — RegistryEntry has no field that could hold manual content. This path only ever ingests a document the user already holds, into the user's own index.

slides.kicker: The last mile is a folder
slides.text: The shop bought the manual. We just make the copy it already owns as findable as the factory's — page-exact, marker on the ink, same two taps.
slides.sub: Fifty-three thousand rows of order, and the one that matters is yours. *Don't trust the AI. Trust the manual — including the one you already paid for.*
notes: The mechanic's document is metered by the hour, and it always will be. So we don't fight it.

If asked what we built today: api/app/dropbox_sync.py — the poller, the webhook with signature verification, the path→vehicle resolver, the ingest hand-off, /dropbox/config|status|sync|webhook — plus 32 tests and api/tools/dropbox_report.py, which generates the chaos evidence from live data so the numbers cannot drift.
Two lines in existing files: one router include, one settings line. Nothing else was touched.

items: Do not say the folder sync is connected. It is built, tested against a mocked Dropbox, and deploying — /api/dropbox/* is not in the live OpenAPI.

Do not say cross-tenant dedupe exists — the content hash is stored, the dedupe is not built.
Do not say "53,557 manuals". They are rows. Then say 14,770 distinct PDFs.
